title: observability: token-level cost/latency + tracing dashboards + alert tuning
author: Evan Lee
release_notes: Adds token-level cost and latency dashboards, augments tracing spans with token metadata, and tunes alerts to reduce noisy paging. No customer-visible API changes.
description:
Context: Customers and internal SREs asked for improved visibility into per-token cost and latency regressions, and better tracing correlation between request spans and KV/cache behavior. This PR wires token-level metrics into our ingestion pipeline, adds Grafana dashboards that join metrics/traces for easy incident triage, and adjusts several alert thresholds to reduce noise.

What this change does:
- Emit token-level cost and latency metrics (per-request aggregates + percentile histograms) from the serving runtime.
- Annotate tracing spans (request, decode, model_infer, kv_cache_hit/miss) with token counts and cost estimates.
- Add three Grafana dashboards: Token Cost & Latency Overview, Token KV Cache Heatmap, Token Tracing Correlation.
- Update alert rules: reduce alerts for p95 token-latency spike to 5 occurrences in 15m, add a targeted alert for sustained kv_cache_miss ratio > 10% on dedicated pools, and suppress noisy low-volume routes.
- Backfill helper scripts to compute per-customer token cost correction for historical dashboards.

Checklist:
- [x] Emit metrics with stable names and unit tests for metric formatting.
- [x] Trace instrumentation added and smoke-tested locally.
- [x] Grafana JSON models added and verified in staging.
- [x] Alert rules reviewed with SRE and tuned to avoid chatty pages.
- [x] Migration/rollout plan documented and gradual rollout configured (15% -> 50% -> 100%).

Testing & rollout:
- Unit tests for metric serialization and tag propagation included.
- End-to-end smoke tests executed in staging (sample traffic, compare cost estimation vs ground truth).
- Canary rollout: enabled for 15% of traffic for 24h, then 50% for 48h before full rollout.

Notes & caveats:
- Cost estimation uses current pricing profiles; if pricing changes we will run a reaggregation job.
- Traces add ~3% overhead in high-throughput paths; slow path traced only when sampling or when latency > p95.
- We use an opt-in environment variable to enable per-customer backfilled dashboards to avoid PII exposure during backfill.

Liam O'Connor (reviewer): Noted potential performance regression from trace tagging. Requested benchmarks.\nEvan: Ran microbenchmarks in perf-canary and found ~3% CPU overhead at 95th percentile; added config flag to enable detailed trace tagging only for sampled traces or slow requests.

Diego Ruiz (SRE): Reviewed alert tuning; recommended 5/15m suppression for low-volume routes and sanity-check thresholds for dedicated pools.\nEvan: Updated alert rules and added suppression list in token_latency_alerts.yml.
